input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: Section 20(h) is the only governing-law/venue provision in the Agreement (no arbitration clause appears anywhere). It selects the laws of Nova Scotia and Canada with the courts of Nova Scotia, which is neither the preferred New York position nor any accepted fallback (Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London), so it fails the fallback on a material term. Venue is non-exclusive rather than exclusive foreign venue, so this is a deviation rather than walk-away. We have replaced only the jurisdiction and forum words with New York law and exclusive New York County state and federal courts, with a carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief, leaving the remainder of the sentence structure intact.

proposal.summary: Replace Nova Scotia governing law and non-exclusive venue with New York law and exclusive New York County courts
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, so we have replaced the Nova Scotia law and non-exclusive Nova Scotia venue, preserving a carve-out only for temporary injunctive relief. Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London would be acceptable fallbacks.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, except that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
